summary: Bettina Bäumer is an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Salzburg and under Lakshman Joo. She served as Director of the Alice Boner Institute and Abhinavagupta Research Library, Professor at the University of Vienna, and Fellow at IIAS.
Bettine Birge is a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology. She completed her Ph.D. at Columbia University under William Theodore de Bary and was a visiting scholar at Academia Sinica in 1994.
Betty Heimann (1888–1961) was an Indologist and philosopher. She studied at Bonn, Kiel, and Halle-Wittenberg, and held posts at Halle-Wittenberg (~1923–1933), SOAS (~1936–1945), Hamburg, and Kiel.
Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya is a scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. His main posts include Dean at Lumbini Buddhist University and Chairman at the Lotus Research Centre.
Bhadriraju Krishnamurti (1928–2012) worked in linguistics and Indology. He was a professor at Osmania University (~1962–1986) and held a post at the Institute for Advanced Study (~1975–1976).
Bhagavan Das (1869–1958) was a scholar in philosophy and Indology who earned an M.A. from the University of Calcutta. He served as Honorary Secretary at Central Hindu College (~1898–1914).
Bhagirath Prasad Tripathi (born 1935) is an Indologist and linguist. He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, including head of the Research Department as attested in 1989.

Bhajagovinda Ghosh works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 1994, he held posts as Assistant Director at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and editorial board member for the Bulletin of Tibetology.

Bharat Bhushan Vidyalankar is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, University of Delhi, and Agra University. He held posts at Kendriya Hindi Sansthan and Sandhaan (1991).

Bhikkhu Anālayo is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Ceylon, University of Marburg, and under Bhikkhu Bodhi, and held posts at Dharma Drum Buddhist College, University of Hamburg, and Sri Lanka International Buddhist Academy.

Bhikkhu Bodhi is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Brooklyn College and Claremont Graduate University, and under Balangoda Ananda Maitreya and Nyanaponika Thera. He served as editor at the Buddhist Publication Society and held a post at Chuang Yen Monastery.

Bhikkhu Pāsādika (born 1939) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at Magadh University. His academic posts include Professor at the University of Marburg (~1993), as well as positions at Kassel and Bergen.

Bhikkhunī Dhammadinnā is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Her academic career includes posts at Dharma Drum Buddhist College, where she was an assistant researcher in 2012, and the Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts.
Bhuvan Chandel is a philosopher and Indologist. She served as a professor at Panjab University (attested 2003) and as Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (~2004–2007).

Bimal Krishna Matilal (1935–1991) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Calcutta and Harvard under W.V.O. Quine and Dagfinn Føllesdal, later holding posts at Toronto, All Souls College, and Oxford as Spalding Professor.

Bindeshwari Prasad Sinha (1919–2002) was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who earned his Ph.D. from the University of London. He was a long-serving professor at Patna University (~1948–1982) and joint director at Kashi Prasad Jayaswal Research Institute.

Bing Chen is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He served as a professor at Sichuan University from around 1987 and held a post at the Chengdu Academy of Social Sciences attested in 1993.
Bintao Ma is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. Ma completed an MA at Peking University in 2008 and a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under Xueyu, attested in 2015.

Biraja Sankar Guha (1894–1961) was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Scottish Church College, Calcutta, and Harvard. He held posts at Calcutta, the Zoological Survey of India (~1927–1945), and the Ethnographic Survey of India.

Birgit Kellner is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She earned her doctorate at Hiroshima University under Shoryu Katsura, and has held posts at the University of Vienna and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.
